observed_original_abi.return_semantics: 0x0067e6c8 MOV EAX,ESI puts the receiver in EAX on the single exit path, taken by both the gated and the ungated path. This CONTRADICTS the persisted SDK/Ghidra signature, which declares 'void App::cCheatManager::func3Ch(cCheatManager * this, int param_2)' and prints the decompiler warning 'Unknown calling convention'. The reconstruction follows the listing and returns the receiver. Whether any consumer reads EAX is unproven: the only inbound reference to the function is its vtable slot, and no call site of that slot is known, so 'returns the receiver' is a statement about the machine, not a proven API contract.

ordinary_stack_arguments.note: 0x0067e6b8 TEST byte ptr [ESP + 0x8],0x1 addresses entry_ESP+0x4 because PUSH ESI at 0x0067e6b0 is the only outstanding frame change and 0x0067e2b0 pushes nothing and ends in a plain RET at 0x0067e301. The test is on the low BYTE, so only bit 0 of the word is given meaning.

corroboration.decompiler_vs_listing: disagreement, and the listing wins. The persisted decompilation reads 'TEST ((uint)this & 1)' and gates on `this`, which is impossible: the instruction is F6 44 24 08 01, a byte test of the stack slot at [ESP+0x8], i.e. entry_ESP+0x4, and the gate word is the function's only ordinary argument. The same decompilation also prints `return;` against a declared void signature while the listing writes EAX at 0x0067e6c8. The reconstruction is built from the 11-instruction listing and the raw bytes, and the decompiler caveats are recorded rather than reproduced.
decompiler_caveats: The decompiler prints the gate as a test of `this`; the listing shows the low byte of the first stack argument. This is the single most consequential difference and the reason the briefing's null decompilation was not usable as-is.
The declared return type is void; the listing writes the receiver into EAX on the only exit path.

The decompiler's 'WARNING: Unknown calling convention' is consistent with a __thiscall entry that has no resolved prototype: __thiscall with a callee-cleaned stack argument is exactly RET 0x4 with the receiver in ECX.
gaps: No ABI projection was persisted for this target (briefing evidence.missing_sections lists ABI as absent). The ABI in this sidecar is derived from the listing, and the derivation is spelled out instruction by instruction in observed_original_abi.

No callers, globals, types, fields or vtable slots were persisted by the orchestrator either; the callee chain, the two globals and the vtable slot were obtained from the live bridge during this session and are cited individually above.

unresolved_questions: What does the gate word mean beyond bit 0? The listing tests one bit and says nothing about the other 31, and the two callees receive the receiver rather than the word, so the word's producer is the only place its meaning could be read.

Is 0x0067e2b0 a destructor? It calls vtable slot +0x10 of the object at +0x14 and then writes &PTR_purecall_0141b5ac into the receiver, which is the MSVC vptr-reset shape a base destructor performs, but the listing names nothing and the only inbound reference is this call site.
What is the object at receiver+0x14, and what does its vtable slot +0x10 do?
What is 0x00926fd0, the routine 0x009276c0 brackets with the lock at global+0x4e4, and what does it do with the receiver it is handed?
What are the two import slots 0x013cc2d8 and 0x013cc2dc? The database resolves no external location for either, so no API name is claimed.
Is the returned EAX consumed by anyone? The only inbound reference to the function is the vtable slot at 0x01401900, and no call site of that slot is known.

Which class owns vtable 0x014018b0, and is it related to the 0x01401b74 table that holds the sibling entries? The table mixes code and non-code words and SporeApp.exe has no RTTI, so the hierarchy is not established.
What are the non-code words 0x00ff0420, 0x00fcc210 and 0x00ab30c0 doing in slots 7, 12 and 9 of that table?
runtime_gates: The function is only reachable through vtable slot 20, so observing it at all requires a live cCheatManager constructed by 0x0067e100 (which stores 0x014018b0) and a caller that dispatches that slot.
The branch is inert unless the gate word has bit 0 set; a differential run that passes an even word will exercise only the teardown path.
The teardown path requires receiver+0x14 to be non-null before the indirect call at 0x0067e2e1 can happen at all.
notes: Reconstructed from the 11-instruction body plus the listings of its two direct callees and the one callee they reach. The reconstruction is total for this body: every instruction, displacement, branch, register and return of 0x0067e6b0..0x0067e6cc is accounted for, and nothing is asserted beyond it. The body is unusually clean for this class -- it loads no receiver field at all, so the header's receiver layout exists only to name what the callees read, and each such field is commented with the listing line that fixes it. Both callees are routed through a port table so the model test can substitute stubs; the VA is kept in the port field names and no pointer value is invented. Where the machine and the persisted SDK signature disagree (the return type, and the decompiler's misattributed gate) the machine is followed and the disagreement is recorded in corroboration.
